audit.summary: Proposition3.2 has the opposite characteristic velocity to its own gradient-flow definition; Lemma2.2 reverses the optimal coupling arguments in its first-order limit. Complete one-dimensional examples satisfy the hypotheses and contradict both printed formulas. Corrections are verified at the declared scope; no failure of the central local convergence theorem established.

proposition.claim:
Proposition 3.2 (p. 20) assumes that \(\phi\) is twice continuously differentiable and satisfies Assumptions 1–3. For a gradient flow \((\mu_t)_{t\geq0}\), it sets \[V_t(s,\omega)=(0,G_{\mu_t}(s,\omega)),\qquad
 \dot X_t=V_t\circ X_t,\quad X_0=\operatorname{Id},\] and asserts \(\mu_t=(X_t)_\#\mu_0\). The sign is confirmed by the actual source image; it conflicts with the continuity equation in Definition 3.2.

d=p=1,Omega=R,phi(omega,x)=omega is C-infinity and satisfies Assumptions1-3; compact dataset delta_(0,0), smooth nonnegative half-square loss; all measures ds tensor delta_a have finite second moment.

Equation reference: eq:printed. The first assertion of Lemma 2.2 (p. 15) takes \(\gamma_t^h\in\Pi_o^{\mathrm{Leb}}(\mu_{t+h},\mu_t)\) and claims \[
 \left(\pi^1,\pi^2,\frac{\pi^3-\pi^2}{h}\right)_\#\gamma_t^h
 \longrightarrow (\pi^1,\pi^2,v_t)_\#\mu_t
 \quad\hbox{in }W_2 .\] Here \(v_t\) is the minimal tangent field from Proposition 2.4. The stated order of the measures and the displayed signs were checked on the source images.

I=(0,1),Omega=R,mu_t=ds tensor delta_t; COT distance|t-u|,locally absolutely continuous, unique minimal tangent v_t=1.
